claims.text: An ML-accelerated ab initio framework using moment-tensor potentials refined with a minimal AIMD dataset can accurately predict fusion and high-temperature thermodynamic properties.
The proposed framework can calculate solid- and liquid-phase free energies while preserving vibrational entropy, anharmonicity, and electron–vibration coupling effects.
The proposed framework will cost substantially less than both explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD workflows.
Relevant simpler elemental and binary cases have already been benchmarked sufficiently to motivate extension to selected high-entropy alloys.
Moment-tensor potentials can capture the local bonding environments needed by the proposed thermodynamic calculations.
Moment-tensor potentials can capture anharmonic vibrational features in both solid and liquid phases.
Calibration using a minimal, targeted set of AIMD samples will preserve the important free-energy contributions in both phases.
Vibrational and anharmonic effects are significant near the fusion transition.
The method will first be validated on elemental and binary systems near their melting transitions.
Limited high-fidelity AIMD training data are sufficient for the ML model to interpolate phase free energies.
Vibrational and configurational entropy are important thermodynamic contributions in the targeted alloy systems.
Training on limited AIMD data will retain electron–vibration coupling effects.
The resulting solid–liquid free-energy differences will be comparable to those from explicit AIMD.
Phase free energies, heat capacities, and transition temperatures will deviate by no more than roughly 10% from AIMD or TOR-TILD results.
The proposed framework will reduce computation time by at least one order of magnitude relative to explicit AIMD.
The proposed framework will match or exceed TOR-TILD speed, especially for multicomponent systems.
TOR-TILD slows substantially as multicomponent complexity increases.
Explicit AIMD and TOR-TILD accurately capture vibrational entropy and anharmonic effects and therefore provide suitable baselines.
Extension of the method to multicomponent high-entropy alloys has not yet been rigorously benchmarked.
Deviation exceeding approximately 10% from explicit AIMD or TOR-TILD phase free energies or derived observables over the targeted temperature range will falsify the hypothesis.
